purpose: Micafungin is used to treat serious fungal infections in the body, especially those caused by a fungus called Candida. It is also used to prevent fungal infections in people who have weakened immune systems, such as those receiving bone marrow transplants. Your doctor will give this medication to you through an IV (intravenous) line in a hospital or clinic setting.
how_it_works: Micafungin works by attacking the outer wall of the fungus, which is like its protective shell. Without this wall, the fungus cannot survive and eventually dies. Think of it like removing the bricks from a building — without them, the structure falls apart. This way, it stops the infection from spreading in your body.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and fever. You might also notice redness, swelling, or discomfort at the IV site. Some people experience low potassium or magnesium levels in their blood, which your care team will monitor closely.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as this medicine can sometimes affect these organs. Let your healthcare team know right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness, as these could be signs of liver problems. Also inform your doctor about all medications you are taking and if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: Micafungin is given once a day through an IV infusion that usually takes about one hour. The exact dose depends on your weight, the type of infection being treated, and your overall health. Your doctor or nurse will decide the right dose for you and administer it in a medical setting.
